items.text:
GOLDMAN SACHS LANCIA DICHIARAZIONE DI DOOMSDAY: I BOND USA NON HANNO ACQUIRENTI

Goldman Sachs ha appena ammesso che il lungo termine del mercato dei Treasury USA è “completamente privo di offerte”.
dice che quasi nessuno è ansioso di acquistare i titoli a lungo termine del governo statunitense (quelli da 10 a 30 anni). Quindi i tassi di interesse su di essi continuano a salire oltre il 5%. Il Tesoro ne sta riacquistando alcuni da sé per mantenere il mercato in movimento e ha definito le condizioni appiccicose. Il Giappone sta vendendo alcuni titoli detenuti. Il post avverte che se i titoli a breve termine perdessero acquirenti dopo, l'intero sistema del debito statunitense potrebbe bloccarsi.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon is known for pushing his employees hard. A quote circulating under his name takes that reputation to its logical extreme, suggesting that a full head of hair is evidence of not putting in enough effort.

Goldman Sachs junior bankers famously surveyed themselves in 2021 and reported working 95-hour weeks and deteriorating physical health. Solomon told them to come back to the office anyway. Does this quote surprise you coming from him?

items.author: Stockstoearn
items.text:
According to its latest 13F filing, Goldman Sachs bought 4,886,103 Nike (NKE) shares during Q2, valued at about $200 MILLION as of June 30.

Goldman held 12,453,144 Nike shares at the end of Q2, currently worth approximately $421 MILLION.

The stock has fallen to its lowest level since September 2013 and is currently down more than 17% since June 30 after Q1 FY27 revenue missed estimates. 

Shares of Nike have plunged more than 80% from their all-time high of $179.10 reached in November 2021 to $33.87, wiping out more than $210 BILLION in market capitalization. 

For the full fiscal year 2027, Nike expects revenue to decline by a high-single-digit percentage and projected adjusted EPS between $1.15 and $1.35, falling well short of prior analyst forecasts.

items.text:
BREAKING: On Sept. 29, Goldman Sachs analyst Eric Sheridan reiterated a Buy rating and a $220 price target on SpaceX (SPCX), implying more than 46% upside from current levels. 

At $220 per share, SpaceX’s market cap would be approximately $3 trillion.

Goldman views SpaceX as exceptionally well-positioned to scale across space launch/reusability, broadband connectivity (Starlink), and space-based AI infrastructure and compute platforms. 

A cornerstone of Goldman’s valuation is SpaceX’s transformation into an AI infrastructure giant. 

The firm projects that SpaceX’s space-based AI compute revenue will experience near a 100-fold surge, rising exponentially by 2030.

Goldman models total company revenue growing to $474 billion by 2030, which is expected to expand adjusted EBITDA to $352 billion by the same year.

GOLDMAN SACHS JUST LEAKED ITS NEXT CEO – AND WALL STREET IS ALREADY FREAKING OUT

The boardroom at Goldman Sachs is quietly orchestrating a massive power shift that could reshape the bank forever. According to a bombshell report, a succession plan is in motion to replace CEO David Solomon with COO John Waldron as early as next year. Solomon, who survived a DJ scandal, partner revolts, and a $7 billion consumer lending disaster, is finally ready to hand over the reins. But the story doesn't end there. Waldron's promotion will trigger a high-stakes scramble for the No. 2 spot, with top executives already jockeying for position. And the timeline? That's where things get really interesting. The exact date is still up in the air, but insiders say the board could approve the move in just months. What happens next will send shockwaves through the entire financial world.

items.text:
🚨 GOLDMAN SACHS DROPS DOOMSDAY STATEMENT: U.S. BONDS HAVE NO BUYERS

Goldman Sachs just admitted the long end of U.S. Treasury market is “totally bidless.”

Translation: almost nobody wants the 10- to 30-year debt the U.S. is trying to sell.

No buyers. None. Zero.

While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tells Congress we’re in an “illiquid period,” doubles then triples long-bond buybacks, taps the General Treasury Account to fund it and openly says “I am the house.”

Yields are surging anyway. The 10-year has pushed toward 5.3% and the 30-year is even higher, levels not seen in years while Japan, one of the biggest foreign holders, keeps selling Treasuries and bringing money home.

This was exactly warned by Japan’s @yutokanzakireal that the measures being prepared by Bank of Japan will affect the lives of billions of people and apologized to people of the West. 

Soon after, Scott Bessent intervened and effectively took over BoJ operations which Japanese policymakers heavily criticized.

If the same ”bidless” condition hits the short-dated treasuries market, the entire U.S. debt market (and global) collapses.

The U.S. debt crisis will turn into a global liquidity crisis.
